profile.feeling: The week starts again — alarm clocks, school, work.

examples.tr: On Monday I go to school.

synonyms.nuance: lǐbàiyī: Monday — southern and older speech

etymology.text: 星期 ‘week’ + 一: ‘week-day 一’ — the days are numbered from Monday.
etymology.src: morphemes: 星期 + 一 (Wiktionary (kaikki.org) character entries)

funFacts: Greek Δευτέρα ‘second’, Hebrew יוֹם שֵׁנִי ‘second day’ and Arabic الاثنين ‘the second’ count from Sunday — Chinese counts from Monday: 星期一 ‘week-one’.
pitfalls: No word for ‘on’: 星期一我工作 / 我星期一工作 — 在星期一 is bookish, and the day never goes at the end (*我工作星期一).
Monday is ONE in Chinese but ‘second’ in Greek: don’t translate Δευτέρα as *星期二.
subtleties: Only Sunday has a name (星期天 / 星期日); Monday to Saturday are just numbers 1–6.

profile.feeling: An ordinary weekday, the week in full swing.

examples.tr: Do you have time on Tuesday?

synonyms.nuance: lǐbài’èr: Tuesday — southern and older speech

etymology.text: 星期 ‘week’ + 二: ‘week-day 二’ — the days are numbered from Monday.
etymology.src: morphemes: 星期 + 二 (Wiktionary (kaikki.org) character entries)

funFacts: Russian вторник (from второй ‘second’) and Chinese 星期二 ‘week-two’ agree: both count from Monday. Greek Τρίτη ‘third’ counts from Sunday.
pitfalls: It is 星期二 with 二, never *星期两: 两 is only for counting things (两个人), not for names and order.
subtleties: ‘Every Tuesday’ is 每个星期二 or, in writing, 每周二.

profile.feeling: Midweek — halfway to the weekend.

examples.tr: On Wednesday afternoon I have no classes.

examples.text: 今天不是星期三，是星期四。
examples.py: Jīntiān bú shì xīngqīsān, shì xīngqīsì.

synonyms.nuance: lǐbàisān: Wednesday — southern and older speech

etymology.text: 星期 ‘week’ + 三: ‘week-day 三’ — the days are numbered from Monday.
etymology.src: morphemes: 星期 + 三 (Wiktionary (kaikki.org) character entries)

funFacts: German Mittwoch ‘mid-week’ and Russian среда (‘middle’) name Wednesday after its place in the week; Chinese just counts: 3.
pitfalls: The number after 星期 names the day (星期三 ‘Wednesday’); a number before it counts weeks: 三个星期 ‘three weeks’.
subtleties: In writing and on timetables 周三 is common: 周三下午.

profile.feeling: Almost there — the week tipping towards Friday.

examples.tr: On Thursday I go to the supermarket.

examples.py: Xīngqīsì wǎnshang nǐ zài jiā ma?
examples.tr: Are you home on Thursday evening?

synonyms.nuance: lǐbàisì: Thursday — southern and older speech

etymology.text: 星期 ‘week’ + 四: ‘week-day 四’ — the days are numbered from Monday.
etymology.src: morphemes: 星期 + 四 (Wiktionary (kaikki.org) character entries)

funFacts: Russian четверг (from четвёртый ‘fourth’) is Chinese 星期四 ‘week-four’; Greek Πέμπτη, Hebrew יוֹם חֲמִישִׁי and Arabic الخميس all say ‘fifth’.
pitfalls: Listen for the tone: 星期四 xīngqīsì (4th tone) is Thursday; 十 shí (2nd tone) is ‘ten’.
subtleties: With days and dates 是 can drop: 今天星期四 ‘today is Thursday’ — the time word itself is the predicate.

profile.feeling: The end of the working week — evenings out, plans for the weekend.

examples.text: 星期五晚上我们去饭馆吃饭。
examples.py: Xīngqīwǔ wǎnshang wǒmen qù fànguǎn chīfàn.
examples.tr: On Friday evening we go out to a restaurant.

examples.text: 下个星期五是我的生日。
examples.py: Xià ge xīngqīwǔ shì wǒ de shēngrì.

synonyms.nuance: lǐbàiwǔ: Friday — southern and older speech

etymology.text: 星期 ‘week’ + 五: ‘week-day 五’ — the days are numbered from Monday.
etymology.src: morphemes: 星期 + 五 (Wiktionary (kaikki.org) character entries)

funFacts: Greek Παρασκευή ‘preparation’ (for the Sabbath), Arabic الجمعة ‘the gathering’ (Friday prayer; Turkish cuma comes from it), Russian пятница ‘fifth’ — Chinese 星期五 ‘week-five’ agrees with the Russian.
pitfalls: ‘Next Friday’ is 下个星期五 (or 下星期五), ‘last Friday’ 上个星期五: 下 ‘down’ is the future, 上 ‘up’ the past.
subtleties: 星期五晚上 ‘Friday evening’: the bigger unit comes first, as in dates.

profile.feeling: No school, no office — the first day of the weekend.

examples.tr: On Saturday we go to the park.
What time do you get up on Saturday?

examples.text: 星期六和星期天是周末。
examples.tr: Saturday and Sunday are the weekend.

synonyms.nuance: lǐbàiliù: Saturday — southern and older speech

etymology.text: 星期 ‘week’ + 六: ‘week-day 六’ — the days are numbered from Monday.
etymology.src: morphemes: 星期 + 六 (Wiktionary (kaikki.org) character entries)

funFacts: Greek Σάββατο, Hebrew שַׁבָּת, Arabic السَّبْت, Russian суббота and German Samstag all come from the Hebrew Sabbath; Chinese simply says ‘week-six’.
pitfalls: 星期六 is the last numbered day: there is no *星期七 — Sunday is 星期天 / 星期日.
subtleties: 礼拜六 is heard in the south (Shanghai) and in older speech.

profile.feeling: A slow day — family lunch, a walk in the park.

examples.tr: On Sundays we go to Grandma’s.

examples.text: 今天是星期天，超市开门吗？
examples.py: Jīntiān shì xīngqītiān, chāoshì kāimén ma?
examples.tr: It’s Sunday today — is the supermarket open?

synonyms.nuance: lǐbàitiān: Sunday — ‘service day’, southern and older speech

etymology.text: 星期 ‘week’ + 天: 天 ‘day’ — the one day of the week with a name, not a number.
etymology.src: morphemes: 星期 + 天 (Wiktionary (kaikki.org) character entries)

funFacts: Greek Κυριακή ‘the Lord’s day’, Russian воскресенье ‘resurrection’, Turkish pazar ‘market’, German Sonntag ‘sun-day’ — Chinese calls it the ‘week-day’ (天 ‘day’).
pitfalls: *星期七 does not exist: Sunday is 星期天 (spoken) or 星期日 (written).
subtleties: 星期天 is the everyday spoken form; 星期日 is used on calendars and forms, 周日 on timetables.

profile.feeling: Sunday as it is printed — calendars, opening hours, forms.

examples.py: Zhège yuè yǒu wǔ ge xīngqīrì.

etymology.text: 星期 ‘week’ + 日: 日 ‘day’ — the one day of the week with a name, not a number.
etymology.src: morphemes: 星期 + 日 (Wiktionary (kaikki.org) character entries)

funFacts: 日 is both ‘sun’ and ‘day’ (日出 ‘sunrise’); German Sonntag and English Sunday are named after the sun.
pitfalls: In conversation 星期日 can sound stiff; with friends say 星期天.
subtleties: Forms, timetables and calendars use 星期日 or 周日.

lexemes.role: week — in the day names 星期一 … 星期六 and 星期几 ‘which day?’ (S14); ‘week’ as a unit of time is the topic of S15

profile.feeling: The seven-day round: 星期一 … 星期天, and ‘which day is it?’.

senses.def: day of the week (with a number: 星期三; in 星期几 ‘which day?’)

examples.py: Yí ge xīngqī yǒu qī tiān.
Wǒ xià ge xīngqī qù Běijīng.
examples.tr: I’m going to Beijing next week.

synonyms.nuance: zhōu: week — more written (一周, 每周, 下周)
lǐbài: week — ‘(church) service’, southern and older speech (下礼拜)

etymology.text: 星 ‘star’ + 期 ‘set time, period’. Wiktionary also lists an old literary sense, the Qixi festival (the night two star-lovers meet); ‘week’ is the modern sense.
etymology.src: Wiktionary (kaikki.org)

funFacts: 礼拜 ‘(religious) service’ is a colloquial word for the week, and 礼拜天 ‘service day’ is Sunday.
pitfalls: 星期 + number names a day (星期三 ‘Wednesday’); number + 个 + 星期 counts weeks (三个星期 ‘three weeks’).
‘Which day is it?’ is 今天星期几？ — the question word 几 takes the place of the number.
subtleties: 星期 is more spoken, 周 more written: 下个星期 / 下周 ‘next week’.

profile.feeling: Saturday and Sunday — sleeping in, friends, a trip out of town.

examples.tr: What are you doing at the weekend?
This weekend we are going to Beijing.
At weekends the supermarket is crowded.

synonyms.nuance: shuāngxiūrì: the two days off (Saturday and Sunday) — official language

etymology.text: 周 ‘week’ + 末 ‘end’: ‘week-end’, built exactly like English weekend and German Wochenende.
etymology.src: morphemes: 周 + 末 (Wiktionary (kaikki.org) character entries)

funFacts: Greek says Σαββατοκύριακο ‘Saturday-Sunday’; Chinese copies the English idea instead: 周 ‘week’ + 末 ‘end’.
pitfalls: ‘At the weekend’ needs no ‘at’: 周末我在家 — *在周末 is only for written style.
subtleties: 周末愉快！ ‘Have a nice weekend!’ is the usual Friday goodbye.

lexemes.measureNone: 天 is itself a counter: 三天 ‘three days’ (no 个)

profile.feeling: The day — and the sky above it.

examples.py: Yí ge xīngqī yǒu qī tiān.
Wǒ zài Běijīng dāi le sān tiān.
examples.tr: I stayed in Beijing for three days.

examples.py: Tiān shang yǒu hěn duō xīngxing.
examples.tr: There are many stars in the sky.

phrases.tr: there is no banquet under heaven that does not end
phrases.meaning: all good things come to an end; every gathering must part

synonyms.nuance: rì: day — written (三日, 日期)

etymology.text: In the oracle bones a standing man (大) with a big mark on his head: ‘top (of the head)’ → ‘sky’ → ‘day’.
etymology.src: Wiktionary (kaikki.org)

funFacts: 天 is both ‘sky’ and ‘day’; 天安门 is the ‘Gate of Heavenly Peace’.
pitfalls: 天 counts by itself — no measure word: 三天 ‘three days’, not *三个天 (compare 三个星期, 三个月).
subtleties: 天天 ‘day-day’ means ‘every day’, like 每天.

profile.feeling: The dark hours — quiet streets, everybody asleep.

senses.def: at night, in the night (the late hours)

examples.py: Tā yèli liǎng diǎn huí jiā.
examples.tr: He came home at two in the night.

collocations.tr: midnight, the middle of the night

synonyms.nuance: wǎnshang: evening and night until bedtime — the everyday word
bànyè: the middle of the night

etymology.text: 夜 ‘night’ + 里 ‘in’: ‘in the night’. 夜 goes back to Proto-Sino-Tibetan *ja-n ‘night’.
etymology.src: Wiktionary (kaikki.org)

funFacts: 夜宵 is the late-night snack — skewers and noodles after ten.
pitfalls: ‘Good night’ is 晚安, not *夜里好.
‘Tonight’ (this evening) is 今天晚上; 今天夜里 is the small hours of tonight.
subtleties: 晚上 covers the evening and the night until you sleep; 夜里 is the dark hours after that.

profile.feeling: Early morning — getting up, breakfast, the way to work.

examples.tr: In the morning I drink coffee.
Tomorrow morning we go to Beijing.

synonyms.nuance: zǎochen: morning, early morning — a little more written
shàngwǔ: the morning until noon (the working morning)

etymology.text: 早 ‘early’ + 上 (as in 晚上): ‘the early part of the day’.
etymology.src: morphemes: 早 + 上 (Wiktionary (kaikki.org) character entries)

funFacts: 早！ alone is a quick ‘morning!’ among colleagues.
pitfalls: 早上好 is the greeting (S02); ‘in the morning’ is just 早上 before the verb: 我早上喝咖啡.
subtleties: 早上 is the early morning (getting up, breakfast); from about nine to twelve it is 上午.

profile.feeling: The working morning — meetings, lessons, until lunch.

examples.tr: In the morning I’m at the office.

examples.py: Míngtiān shàngwǔ nǐ yǒu shíjiān ma?
examples.tr: Do you have time tomorrow morning?

etymology.text: 上 ‘upper, earlier’ + 午 ‘noon’: ‘the part before noon’.
etymology.src: morphemes: 上 + 午 (Wiktionary (kaikki.org) character entries)

funFacts: 午 is the hour of the horse (11 a.m. – 1 p.m.) in the old twelve-part day: 上午 comes before it, 下午 after it, 中午 is the middle.
pitfalls: Clock times need the part of the day FIRST to be clear: 上午十点 ‘10 a.m.’, 晚上十点 ‘10 p.m.’.
subtleties: 早上 is getting up and breakfast; 上午 is the working morning, until noon.

lexemes.measureNone: a time word: it is not counted with a measure word

profile.feeling: Midday — the lunch break, a short nap.

examples.py: Wǒ zhōngwǔ zài xuéxiào chī wǔfàn.
examples.tr: I have lunch at school at midday.

examples.py: Zhōngwǔ shí'èr diǎn wǒ zài jiā.
examples.tr: At twelve noon I’m at home.

etymology.text: 中 ‘middle’ + 午 ‘noon (the hour of the horse)’.
etymology.src: morphemes: 中 + 午 (Wiktionary (kaikki.org) character entries)

funFacts: Many Chinese take a 午睡 ‘midday nap’ after lunch.
pitfalls: ‘At noon’ is 中午 before the verb; 午饭 is the meal itself, ‘lunch’.
subtleties: 中午 is roughly eleven to one — the lunch break, not only 12:00.

profile.feeling: The afternoon — tea, the second half of the working day.

examples.tr: In the afternoon I’m at home.
What are you doing on Saturday afternoon?

etymology.text: 下 ‘lower, later’ + 午 ‘noon’: ‘after noon’.
etymology.src: morphemes: 下 + 午 (Wiktionary (kaikki.org) character entries)

funFacts: English p.m. is Latin post meridiem ‘after midday’ — exactly 下午 ‘below noon’.
pitfalls: 下午三点 ‘3 p.m.’: the part of the day comes first, then the hour.
subtleties: 下午 lasts until about six; after that it is 晚上.

profile.feeling: Evening and night — dinner, lights on, the day winding down.

senses.def: night (until bedtime): 昨天晚上 ‘last night’

examples.tr: In the evening we eat at home.
What are you doing this evening?
He doesn’t drink coffee at night.

examples.py: Zuótiān wǎnshang wǒ hěn wǎn huí jiā.
examples.tr: Last night I came home late.

synonyms.nuance: yèli: in the night — the late hours

etymology.text: 晚 ‘late; evening’ + 上 (as in 早上).
etymology.src: morphemes: 晚 + 上 (Wiktionary (kaikki.org) character entries)

funFacts: 晚 is both ‘evening’ and ‘late’ — like Spanish tarde ‘afternoon; late’.
pitfalls: ‘Tonight’ is 今天晚上 (written 今晚).
晚上好 is the greeting ‘good evening’; 晚安 ‘good night’ is said when going to bed.
subtleties: 晚上 covers the whole evening and the night until you sleep — English ‘last night’ is usually 昨天晚上.

lexemes.measureNone: a time word: it is not counted with a measure word

profile.feeling: Today — here and now.

examples.tr: I’m not going to school today.

phrases.meaning: don’t put off till tomorrow what you can do today

etymology.text: 今 ‘now, the present’ + 天 ‘day’: ‘this day’.
etymology.src: morphemes: 今 + 天 (Wiktionary (kaikki.org) character entries)

funFacts: Greek σήμερα, German heute and Russian сегодня (сего дня ‘of this day’) are all ‘this day’ — just like 今天.
pitfalls: 今天 goes before the verb, at the start or after the subject: 今天我不去 / 我今天不去 — never at the end (*我不去今天).
subtleties: With days and dates 是 can drop: 今天星期一 ‘today is Monday’.

lexemes.measureNone: a time word: it is not counted with a measure word

profile.feeling: Tomorrow — plans, hopes, ‘see you then’.

etymology.text: 明 ‘bright; next’ + 天 ‘day’: ‘the next day’.
etymology.src: morphemes: 明 + 天 (Wiktionary (kaikki.org) character entries)

funFacts: 明 is sun 日 + moon 月 = ‘bright’; it also means ‘next’: 明年 ‘next year’.
pitfalls: There is no future tense: 明天 alone makes it the future — 明天我去 ‘I’ll go tomorrow’. Don’t add 了.
subtleties: 明天 is also ‘the future’: 更好的明天 ‘a better tomorrow’.

lexemes.measureNone: a time word: it is not counted with a measure word

profile.feeling: Yesterday — just gone, still remembered.

examples.py: Zuótiān wǎnshang nǐ qù nǎli le?
examples.tr: Where did you go last night?

etymology.text: 昨 ‘yesterday’ + 天 ‘day’.
etymology.src: morphemes: 昨 + 天 (Wiktionary (kaikki.org) character entries)

funFacts: The day before yesterday is 前天 ‘front day’ and the day after tomorrow 后天 ‘back day’.
pitfalls: There is no past tense: 昨天 alone places it in the past — 昨天我在家 ‘I was at home yesterday’ (在 and 是 do not change).
subtleties: 昨天晚上 is ‘last night’ (the evening); late in the night is 昨天夜里.

lexemes.measureNone: a time word: it is not counted with a measure word

profile.feeling: Now — this very moment.

etymology.text: 现 ‘to appear, present’ + 在 ‘to be at’: ‘being present’.
etymology.src: morphemes: 现 + 在 (Wiktionary (kaikki.org) character entries)

funFacts: 现在 also names ‘the present’ in grammar books: 现在时 ‘present tense’ — a tense Chinese never marks.
pitfalls: 现在 goes before the verb: 我现在去 ‘I’m going now’ — not *我去现在.
subtleties: 现在 + … + 了 marks a change: 现在他是老师了 ‘now he is a teacher (he wasn’t before)’.

lexemes.measureNone: a time word: it is not counted with a measure word

override.meaning: Wiktionary glosses 以後 as ‘afterwards; after this; from now on; in the future’ — that is the sense ‘later’ taught here

profile.feeling: Later, afterwards — the time that comes behind.

senses.def: after (a time or event): 吃饭以后 (S15)

examples.tr: Later on I want to go to China.
After class I go to the park.

examples.py: Shí diǎn yǐhòu wǒ bù hē kāfēi.
examples.tr: I don’t drink coffee after ten.

synonyms.nuance: zhīhòu: after, afterwards — a little more written (S15)
hòulái: afterwards — about the past only

etymology.text: 以 ‘by, from’ + 后 ‘behind, after’: ‘from then on, after’.
etymology.src: morphemes: 以 + 后 (Wiktionary (kaikki.org) character entries)

funFacts: 以后 and 以前 use the same 后 / 前 as 后面 / 前面 (S12): space and time share words, like German vor / nach (vor dem Haus — vor dem Essen).
pitfalls: 以后 comes AFTER what it refers to: 吃饭以后 ‘after eating’ — the opposite order of English after and German nach.
‘Later’ about the past (‘and then …’) is 后来, not 以后.
subtleties: Alone at the start, 以后 means ‘from now on, in future’: 以后别这样了 ‘don’t do that again’.

profile.feeling: In a bit — after this, later today.

examples.py: Děng yíxià wǒ gěi nǐ dǎ diànhuà.

examples.tr: We’ll go to the supermarket in a bit.

collocations.tr: let’s talk about it in a bit

synonyms.nuance: yíhuìr: in a little while, soon
dāihuìr: in a bit — northern speech

etymology.text: 等 ‘to wait’ + 一下 ‘a moment, once’: ‘wait a moment’ → ‘in a moment, later’.
etymology.src: morphemes: 等 + 一下 (Wiktionary (kaikki.org) character entries)

funFacts: 等一下 shows how Chinese turns verbs into time words: ‘wait a little’ becomes ‘later’.
pitfalls: Said děng yíxià: 一 changes to yí before the 4th tone of 下 (dictionaries write yī).
subtleties: 等一下 is ‘later today, in a little while’; for a far future use 以后.

profile.feeling: Right away — ‘I’m coming!’, ‘we’re nearly there!’.

senses.def: at once, right away, soon, in a minute

examples.tr: The train is about to leave.

etymology.text: From 马背上 ‘on horseback’: the horse was the fastest way to travel, so ‘at once’.
etymology.src: Wiktionary (kaikki.org)

funFacts: 马上 ‘on horseback’ = ‘right away’: in old China nothing was faster than a horse.
pitfalls: 马上 often pairs with 就 … 了: 马上就到了 ‘we’re almost there’.
subtleties: 马上 is elastic: 我马上来 can mean one minute — or twenty.

override.meaning: Wiktionary glosses 一會 as ‘a little while; a moment’; before the verb (一会就来 ‘will come in a moment’) that is the sense ‘soon’ taught here

profile.feeling: A little while — in a moment, back soon.

senses.def: in a moment, soon (before the verb: 一会就来)
a little while (as a length of time, after the verb)

examples.tr: He’ll be here in a moment.

synonyms.nuance: yíhuìr: the same with the Beijing ‘erhua’ ending — the usual northern spoken form
děng yíxià: in a bit, later

etymology.text: 一 ‘one’ + 会 ‘a moment’: ‘one moment’.
etymology.src: morphemes: 一 + 会 (Wiktionary (kaikki.org) character entries)

funFacts: In the north you hear 一会儿 yíhuìr: the 儿 is the ‘erhua’ r-ending of Beijing speech; southern speakers say 一会.
pitfalls: Before the verb 一会 is ‘soon’ (一会就来); after the verb it is ‘a little while’ (等一会).
subtleties: 一会 … 一会 … means ‘now … now …’: 一会冷，一会热 ‘now cold, now hot’.

profile.feeling: Early — the sun just up, the first bus.

examples.py: Wǒmen míngtiān zǎo yìdiǎn qù ba.
examples.tr: Let’s go a bit earlier tomorrow.

examples.py: Nǐ jīntiān lái de hěn zǎo.

phrases.tr: the early bird has worms to eat
phrases.meaning: the early bird catches the worm

synonyms.nuance: tíqián: in advance, ahead of time
zǎozǎo: very early, in good time

etymology.text: Phono-semantic in the bronze inscriptions: 日 ‘sun’ + phonetic 棗 (earlier a drawing borrowed for its sound); the seal-script form was read as ‘sun’ + 甲 ‘first’ — when the sun first rises.
etymology.src: Wiktionary (kaikki.org)

funFacts: 早 ‘early’ gives 早饭 ‘early meal’ = breakfast and 早上 ‘morning’.
pitfalls: After a verb, 早 / 晚 need 得: 你来得很早 ‘you came early’; before a verb add 一点: 早一点去 ‘go a bit earlier’.
subtleties: 早！ alone is a casual ‘good morning’.

profile.feeling: Late — the last bus gone, the lights going out.

examples.text: 现在很晚了，我们回家吧。
examples.py: Xiànzài hěn wǎn le, wǒmen huí jiā ba.
examples.tr: It’s late now — let’s go home.

phrases.tr: to regret not having met earlier
phrases.meaning: said of a new friend you feel you have always known

synonyms.nuance: chí: late — written (迟到 ‘to arrive late’)

etymology.text: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 日 ‘sun’ + phonetic 免; from Proto-Sino-Tibetan *mor ‘night’. Wiktionary compares Spanish tarde, which also means both ‘evening’ and ‘late’.
etymology.src: Wiktionary (kaikki.org)

funFacts: 晚 is both ‘evening’ and ‘late’, like Spanish tarde.
pitfalls: ‘I’m late’ (arriving) is 我来晚了 or 我迟到了 — not *我是晚.
subtleties: 晚 + 了 marks a change: 现在很晚了 ‘it’s got late’.

profile.feeling: Always — every time, without fail (sometimes with a sigh).

examples.tr: In the morning I always drink coffee.

synonyms.nuance: shǐzhōng: from start to finish, throughout

etymology.text: 总 ‘all, always’ + 是 ‘to be’.
etymology.src: morphemes: 总 + 是 (Wiktionary (kaikki.org) character entries)

funFacts: 老是 ‘old-is’ is the grumbling ‘always’: 你老是迟到！
pitfalls: 总是 goes before the verb, after the subject: 我总是喝茶 — never at the end.
A negation follows it: 他总是不吃早饭 ‘he never has breakfast’ (he always doesn’t).
subtleties: Like English ‘always’, 总是 can carry irritation: 你总是这样！ ‘you’re always like this!’

profile.feeling: Often — a habit, a favourite place.

examples.tr: I often go to the park.

synonyms.nuance: jīngcháng: often, regularly — a little more formal
cháng: often — the short form (不常 ‘not often’)

etymology.text: 常 ‘constant, often’ doubled.
etymology.src: morphemes: 常 + 常 (Wiktionary (kaikki.org) character entries)

funFacts: Doubling makes adverbs of frequency: 常 → 常常, 天 → 天天 ‘every day’.
pitfalls: The negation is 不常 ‘not often’ — *不常常 is avoided.
subtleties: 常常 is everyday speech; 经常 sounds more regular and is common in writing.

profile.feeling: Regularly, frequently — a routine.

examples.text: 我经常在这家饭馆吃饭。
examples.py: Wǒ jīngcháng zài zhè jiā fànguǎn chīfàn.
examples.tr: I often eat at this restaurant.

synonyms.nuance: wǎngwǎng: usually, tends to (a pattern from experience)

etymology.text: 经 ‘constant, regular’ + 常 ‘constant’.
etymology.src: morphemes: 经 + 常 (Wiktionary (kaikki.org) character entries)

funFacts: As an adjective 经常 means ‘everyday, regular’: 经常性的工作 ‘routine work’.
pitfalls: 不经常 ‘not often’ is fine; with 常常 it is 不常.
subtleties: 往往 states a tendency known from experience and is not used for the future or for wishes; 经常 can be: 以后我会经常来.

profile.feeling: Sometimes — now and then, it depends.

examples.text: 我有时候坐公共汽车，有时候走路。
examples.py: Wǒ yǒushíhou zuò gōnggòng qìchē, yǒushíhou zǒulù.
examples.tr: Sometimes I take the bus, sometimes I walk.

synonyms.nuance: yǒushí: the same, shorter — also written
ǒu’ěr: occasionally, once in a while

etymology.text: 有 ‘there is’ + 时候 ‘time, moment’: ‘there are times (when)’.
etymology.src: morphemes: 有 + 时候 (Wiktionary (kaikki.org) character entries)

funFacts: Literally ‘there are times’ — like English ‘at times’.
pitfalls: 有时候 goes before the verb or at the very start: 有时候我走路 / 我有时候走路 — not at the end.
subtleties: 有时候 … 有时候 … balances two habits: 有时候喝茶，有时候喝咖啡.

lexemes.role: in the middle of …-ing: the progressive before a verb, 他正在吃饭 (S14)

profile.feeling: Right now, in the middle of it — the action caught as it happens.

senses.def: in the middle of …-ing (progressive, before a verb)

synonyms.nuance: zài: the same, shorter — the everyday progressive

etymology.text: 正 ‘just, exactly’ + 在 ‘to be at’: ‘right at (doing)’.
etymology.src: morphemes: 正 + 在 (Wiktionary (kaikki.org) character entries)

funFacts: 呢 at the end adds ‘right now’: 他在吃饭呢 ‘he’s eating at the moment’.
pitfalls: 正在 does not go with verbs that cannot last (到, 是, 知道): *他正在到 is wrong.
subtleties: 正在 stresses ‘at this very moment’; 在 alone is the everyday form.

lexemes.role: aspect particle: after the verb, a completed action (买了两张票); at the end of the sentence, a new situation (他来了) (S14)

profile.feeling: Done, or changed — the action is complete, the situation is new.

senses.def: (after the verb) completed action: 买了两张票
(at the end) change, new situation: 下雨了, 他来了

examples.py: Wǒ mǎi le liǎng zhāng piào.

profile.synonymsNone: No other word marks completion; 过 marks experience (去过) and 完 ‘to finish’ a result (吃完) — see the grammar page.

etymology.text: 了 liǎo ‘to finish, to be completed’ weakened into the particle le: first the completed action (verb-了), then the new situation (sentence-final 了).
etymology.src: Wiktionary (kaikki.org)

funFacts: The particle 了 le and the verb 了 liǎo ‘to finish’ are one character: 了解 liǎojiě ‘to understand’ keeps the old reading.
pitfalls: 了 is not a past tense: a past habit takes no 了 (以前他常常来), and 了 can refer to the future (明天吃了饭再去 ‘tomorrow I’ll go after eating’).
没 negates without 了: 他没来 ‘he didn’t come’ — never *他没来了.
subtleties: With a bare object, sentence-final 了 sounds more natural than verb-了: 我买票了 ‘I’ve bought the tickets’; verb-了 likes a number: 我买了两张票.

lexemes.role: aspect particle: experience — have (ever) done, 去过北京 ‘have been to Beijing’ (S14)

profile.feeling: Been there, done that — an experience you have had.

senses.def: (after a verb) have ever / once done (experience)
(guò, verb) to cross, to pass, to spend (time): 过生日

examples.tr: Have you ever eaten Chinese food?
How do you celebrate your birthday?

profile.synonymsNone: No other particle marks experience; compare 了 (completion) on the grammar page.

etymology.text: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 辵 ‘walk’ + phonetic 咼 — ‘to pass, to cross’. After a verb: the action has been passed through, i.e. experienced.
etymology.src: Wiktionary (kaikki.org)

funFacts: 过 is the same word as ‘to cross’ (过马路 ‘cross the street’): an experience is something you have ‘crossed’.
pitfalls: Negation keeps 过: 我没去过 ‘I’ve never been’ — unlike 了, which drops after 没.
subtleties: 去过 = been there (and back): an experience; 去了 = went (and may still be there): 他去过北京 vs 他去北京了.

lexemes.role: every, each — 每天 ‘every day’, 每个星期一 ‘every Monday’; usually with 都 before the verb (S14)
